feedback.problem: Which of the following functions is not continuous at $x=2$ but is right-continuous at that point?
feedback.worked_solution:
To determine whether a function $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=2,$ we need to check whether the right-sided limit is equal to the function value.

The function plotted below has a discontinuity at $x=2,$ but is right-continuous at $x=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945035/assets/b0c5521372b10882b6f5357cb678aef1274df935e7626bec930e3e084674ba62.png)

Indeed, we see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x)=1=f(2).
$$

Thus, $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=2.$
